sections.h2: Where do Catoosa County property taxes get paid?
sections.html:
The Catoosa County Tax Commissioner has two offices. The main office is at 796 LaFayette Street in Ringgold, and a satellite office is at 205 Forrest Road in Fort Oglethorpe. The phone number is (706) 965-2571.

Main office hours vary by day: Monday, Wednesday and Friday 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, Tuesday 7:30 am to 5:00 pm, and Thursday 8:30 am to 6:00 pm. The Fort Oglethorpe office runs 8:30 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday. The Fort Oglethorpe office stops title work at 4:45 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and at 5:45 on Thursday.

Property value is handled by the Catoosa County Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street in Ringgold, reachable at 706-965-3772. The assessor's office keeps ownership and appraisal records for more than 28,000 real estate parcels and about 6,900 personal property and mobile home records.

sections.h2: When is the Catoosa County tax bill due, and which cities are on it?
sections.html:
Catoosa County property taxes are generally due by December 20. The county bill also includes the taxes of the City of Ringgold and the City of Fort Oglethorpe, so owners inside those cities do not receive a separate city bill from the tax commissioner.

The tax commissioner's guide to reading a bill explains the taxing districts. District 01 is the unincorporated county, District 02 is the City of Ringgold, and District 03 is the City of Fort Oglethorpe. Voting districts do not match taxing districts, so check the district code on a bill before assuming which millage applies.

  • The due date is the last day payment can be made without interest or penalty.
  • A Notice of Assessment is an estimate and is not a tax bill, and it may not reflect exemptions you qualify for.
  • The sales tax credit on a bill is a saving based on the prior year's local option sales tax proceeds.

Mobile and manufactured homes sitting in the county on January 1 are taxed by April 1, and the location permit is issued at the same time. Missing that deadline adds a 10% penalty, a FiFa and possibly a sale of the home.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Catoosa County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. For 2024, the county posted a deadline of August 9, so that year's window closed in the summer, and the same 45-day rule applies to every notice since.

Appeals can be made three ways: in person at the Tax Assessor's office, by mail to the Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street, Ringgold, Georgia 30736, or online through the assessor's page on the qPublic property site. The first filing must state the method you pick, and the tax commissioner's page lists them as Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration.

The appeal can challenge taxability, value, or uniformity with similar properties. It cannot be based on the amount of tax levied. Mobile home owners who want to declare a different value have 45 days to file with the Board of Tax Assessors, and may go to the Board of Equalization within 21 days of a value change notice.

The county's 2024 announcement also explains why bills can fall even when values rise: the county, the school board and the two city councils calculate a rollback millage rate after the notices go out. A Notice of Assessment uses the previous year's millage rate for its estimate.

sections.h2: How does homestead exemption work in Catoosa County?
sections.html:
Catoosa is a county where the tax commissioner's office, not the assessors, takes the initial homestead application. Georgia law allows filing all year, but the application must be received by April 1 of the year the exemption is first claimed. Later filings apply to the following tax year.

A Georgia ID is required for all homestead exemptions, and first-time homeowners bring a copy of their warranty deed. The Board of Assessors makes the final decision on eligibility, and a denied applicant is notified and has an appeal route. Once granted, the exemption renews automatically until the owner changes residence, ownership or exemption type.

Catoosa County has local exemptions that replace the state amounts when they are larger. The commissioner's site lists regular, veteran and senior exemptions, and a property tax deferral program is described on its own page. Ask the office which one fits your age and situation before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What should I do about unpaid Catoosa County taxes before a sale?
sections.html:
Contact the tax commissioner for the full balance and ask your closing attorney or title company to pay it from the sale proceeds. The commissioner's home page states that if taxes are not paid, the property may be levied upon and ultimately sold, and it links to a Delinquent Tax Sale Information Guide and to a list of excess funds from past tax sales.

Georgia's tax lien attaches to the property as of its January 1 valuation and ranks ahead of other liens, which is why a title company will insist on a payoff. A homeowner who has already received a tax sale notice should call the office right away, because the timing of the sale controls what you can still do.

If you have already sold and a bill arrives for the old house, send it on to the buyer. The notice goes to the owner on record, so make sure the deed is recorded promptly.

sections.h2: What is Catoosa County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Catoosa County is a compact northwest Georgia county of 162 square miles, bordering Hamilton County, Tennessee to the north, Whitfield County to the east and Walker County to the west. Ringgold is the county seat and Fort Oglethorpe is the largest city, with the town of Tunnel Hill and the communities of Graysville, Woodstation, Indian Springs and Lakeview also in the county. It is part of the Chattanooga metropolitan area.

Interstate 75 and U.S. 27 are the main routes, with U.S. 41 and 76 and State Routes 2, 146 and 151 filling in. All of the county is in Catoosa County Public Schools, whose schools include Battlefield, Boynton, Ringgold and Tiger Creek elementary schools and Heritage, Lakeview and Ringgold middle schools. An April 27, 2011 tornado struck Ringgold,.

faqs.q: What day are Catoosa County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Generally December 20. The county bill also carries the City of Ringgold and City of Fort Oglethorpe taxes, so one payment covers all three taxing districts. Check the due date printed on your own bill.

faqs.q: Is a Catoosa County Notice of Assessment a bill?
faqs.a: No. It is a notice of the fair market value the assessors placed on your property, with a tax estimate based on the prior year's millage rate. It may not include exemptions, and a rollback of the millage rate can lower the final bill.

faqs.q: Where do I file a homestead exemption in Catoosa County?
faqs.a: With the Tax Commissioner's office, which takes the initial application in Catoosa. Bring a Georgia ID, and a warranty deed if you are a first-time owner. The application must be received by April 1 to count for that tax year.

faqs.q: How long does a Catoosa County mobile home owner have to pay?
faqs.a: Until April 1 for homes in the county on January 1, with the location permit issued then. A late payment draws a 10% penalty, a FiFa and possibly a sale of the home.

faqs.q: Which Catoosa County office handles an appeal?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street in Ringgold takes appeals in person, by mail or online. You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed, and you must pick Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration when you file.
